Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources and build procedures for the rsgain package. The `source` array fetches a tagged release tarball from the project's official GitHub repository using HTTPS, which is a trusted upstream source. The checksum is provided via `sha512sums`, ensuring integrity verification of the downloaded archive. There are no command substitutions, unescaped interpolations, or executable snippets in the global scope or within `pkgver()`, and no code outside of the `build()` and `package()` functions will execute during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`.

The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will only clone or download sources (in this case, an archive) and source the PKGBUILD to extract metadata, including running `pkgver()` if defined. Here, `pkgver` is static (`pkgver=3.7`), so no dynamic version computation occurs. No network operations, file modifications, or code executions happen at parse time. All dependencies and sources align with standard AUR packaging practices.

Fetching the source archive—even without a SKIPped checksum—does not pose a risk at this stage because extraction does not imply execution, and `--nobuild` prevents any build or install steps. The presence of valid, expected sources and absence of top-level malicious payloads confirms this step is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious behavior during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>
